name: Sarajevo Youth Theatre
description: A theater in the city center that kept staging plays and concerts throughout the siege of 1992 to 1996.

name: Hotel Holiday
description: A yellow hotel opened for the 1984 Winter Olympics, which housed foreign journalists during the siege of Sarajevo.

name: National Museum of Bosnia and Herzegovina
places: National Museum of Bosnia and Herzegovina
description: The country’s oldest museum, founded in 1888. It holds the Sarajevo Haggadah, a medieval illuminated Jewish manuscript.
wikipedia: National Museum of Bosnia and Herzegovina

name: Baščaršija
description: The old Ottoman bazaar, with craft workshops, mosques, and a wooden fountain called the Sebilj in its main square.

name: Zetra Olympic Hall
description: An arena built for the 1984 Winter Olympics. It was burned in the war, and its grounds became a cemetery during the siege.

name: War Childhood Museum
description: A museum of objects and memories from people who were children during the war of 1992 to 1995.

name: Latin Bridge
description: An Ottoman stone bridge over the Miljacka river. The heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne was shot on the corner beside it in 1914.

name: Bridge of Suada and Olga
description: A bridge named for two women shot there at a peace protest on April 5, 1992, often counted as the first victims of the siege.
